topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the learning objectives for the final lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Treatments and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss standard frontline cancer treatment modalities and the clinical limitations imposed by systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cellular Vulnerabilities and DNA Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone signaling, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Oncogene-Targeted Kinase Inhibitors and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail small molecule kinase inhibitors designed to block hyperactive oncogenic drivers and the biological mechanisms through which cancers develop resistance to them.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address targeted antibody therapies that direct receptor inhibition, immune-mediated cytotoxicity, or cytotoxic drug payloads directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Immune Checkpoint Inhibition and T-Cell-Based Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles and modalities of cell-mediated immunotherapy designed to unleash or engineer T-cell responses against tumor antigens.

topics.label: Therapeutic Progress, Persistent Challenges, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the overall progress, persisting therapeutic challenges, and future biological and clinical directions in cancer management.
